_note: Synthetic evaluation ground truth. NEVER expose to production attribution queries. Used only by run_evaluation.py to score algorithm correctness against held-out fixtures.
_label: Synthetic unit evaluation — not real-world field validation.

cases.description: All out-of-range readings fall in H2. No other handoff has out-of-range exposure.
cases.scoring_note: Both primary and naive correctly select EH2 because only one handoff has readings.

cases.description: Excursion spans two handoffs. H2 holds 75% (120 DM) of out-of-range exposure, H3 holds 25% (40 DM). Primary target should select H2.
cases.scoring_note: Naive picks FH1 due to boundary-inclusive match at 10:00:00, missing cumulative exposure entirely.

cases.description: Two handoffs (GH1 and GH2) have exactly equal supported out-of-range exposure (120 DM each). Attribution rank 1 is shared — no unique winner.
cases.scoring_note: Primary detects tie and refuses to declare unique winner. Naive arbitrarily crowns GH1 based on first reading.

cases.description: Logger has +300s clock skew. Breach occurs at 09:56-09:58 UTC (in KH1). Logger clock reports 10:01-10:03 (looks like KH2). Skew correction correctly attributes to KH1.
cases.scoring_note: Primary corrects skew (-300s) and identifies KH1. Naive uses raw timestamp 10:01 and erroneously blames KH2.

cases.description: Only two readings 90 minutes apart (>600s threshold). All segments unsupported. Should return INCONCLUSIVE_INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
cases.scoring_note: Primary abstains with INCONCLUSIVE_INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Naive blindly outputs MH1 without checking data sufficiency.
